rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this round pushes obfuscation coverage up across all seven passes while keeping cost weights moderate for this tiny 1142-byte, 3-function binary. SPLIT gets the highest DiversityGain and lowest cost weights because splitting basic blocks is cheap and amplifies FLA/BCF/IBR by giving them more regions to transform. SUB and ICALL carry the highest SecurityGain since instruction substitution and indirect-call conversion defeat static pattern matching with low correctness risk, which matters for drop_0xx's tight bit-manipulation loop. BCF is weighted toward security but with an elevated RuntimeCost weight so the scheduler spares the hot loop from bogus-control-flow bloat. FLA and IGV diversify control flow and global layout respectively at low risk, and IBR adds basic-block relocation to break block-level signatures, keeping all RuntimeCost weights at or below 0.6 so runtime overhead stays acceptable while correctness, already verified in round 0, remains protected by low CorrectnessRisk weights throughout.
